solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Shrink disadvantage (8)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Shrink' is a verb for DRAW BACK, the phrase; 'disadvantage' is the noun DRAWBACK.

blocks.note: a verb here: to recoil or pull away, a two-word phrase
a noun: a snag or downside

annotation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings: the verb phrase DRAW BACK and the noun DRAWBACK are spelt the same once the space goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonyms both ways: you draw back in fear, and a drawback is the snag in a plan.

entries.clue: Ascend where rocky, time for upper air? (7)

indicatorNotes.rocky: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of ASCEND wobble into a new order

blocks.note: ASCEND rearranged
T is the standard abbreviation for time

annotation.surface: A climber is told that where the rock gets rough, it is time to head up for some air.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Air' here is a tune, not the atmosphere: a descant is the melody sung above the main one, hence 'upper air'.
annotation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody line sung or played above the main tune.

entries.clue: Issue frequently engulfing Lima (5)

indicatorNotes.engulfing: to engulf is to swallow up, so A LOT closes round the L

blocks.note: a lot = frequently, as in 'she travels a lot'
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Something keeps coming out and swamping the Peruvian capital.
annotation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the city, but it is the radio code word for L, which sits between A and LOT.
annotation.definitionFit: To allot is to issue or hand out shares of something.

entries.clue: Requirement for flight as a songbird remarkably maintains power (8,4)

indicatorNotes.remarkably: remarkably suggests something surprising has happened to the letters, so they are rearranged
indicatorNotes.maintains: to maintain is to hold, so the rearranged letters hold P inside them

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
P is the symbol for power in physics

annotation.surface: A bird needs to be remarkably strong to take off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flight' reads as a songbird taking wing, but the definition is about an aeroplane: you need a boarding pass to get on.
annotation.definitionFit: A description rather than a synonym: without this card at the gate, the airline will not let you fly.

entries.clue: Young camper, an islander (5)

blocks.note: a Cub is a junior Scout, the kind who goes camping
taken as written

annotation.surface: A child at camp turns out to come from an island.
annotation.walkthrough: Cubs are the younger branch of the Scouts, famous for camping trips; Cuba supplies the island.
annotation.definitionFit: A Cuban lives on the island of Cuba.

entries.clue: Fine material captured by digital camera (4)

indicatorNotes.captured by: the answer is caught inside the words that follow

blocks.note: digiTAL Camera

annotation.surface: A digital camera photographs some delicate fabric.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine material' sounds like cloth, but talc is a fine powder.
annotation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a very fine powder.

entries.clue: Poorly rated, company style (3,4)

indicatorNotes.Poorly: poorly means badly, so RATED is put together badly

blocks.note: RATED rearranged
Co. is the usual abbreviation for company

annotation.surface: A firm's look has had bad reviews.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poorly rated' reads as a verdict on the company, but 'Poorly' only tells you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the geometric design movement of the 1920s and 30s is one named style among many.

entries.clue: Teams on ship sail around we hear (5)

indicatorNotes.we hear: we hear points to how the words sound, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: to cruise is to sail around on a ship

annotation.surface: Groups aboard a vessel go sailing about.
annotation.walkthrough: The ship picture keeps pulling you towards sailors, which makes CREWS feel like the definition's cousin rather than the sound of 'cruise'.
annotation.definitionFit: Crews are teams, whether on a ship or anywhere else.

entries.clue: Ground dreariest, as a battlefield (8,4)

indicatorNotes.Ground: ground means crushed, as in ground coffee, so the letters are broken up and remade

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A grim patch of earth, bleak as any battlefield.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' reads as land to match the battlefield, but it is the past tense of grind.
annotation.definitionFit: A battlefield is a scene of wreckage, which is what a disaster area is.

entries.clue: Saucy Hispanic moves? (5)

blocks.note: the surface wants cheeky; the setter means 'sauce-like', pointing at a spicy Mexican dip
dance steps from Latin America, the same word as the dip

annotation.surface: Cheeky dance steps from someone of Spanish-speaking heritage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' seems to mean cheeky, but it points to the sauce; 'Hispanic moves' is the dance, and both are salsa.
annotation.definitionFit: Salsa is a Latin dance and also a spicy Latin sauce.

entries.clue: Litres spread on black hair (7)

indicatorNotes.spread: spread means scattered about, so the letters of LITRES are moved around

blocks.note: B is black, as on pencils
LITRES rearranged

annotation.surface: Pouring litres of something over dark hair.
annotation.walkthrough: The rearranged LITRES is placed on B, following it in the across entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: the short stiff sort of hair on a brush or a chin.

entries.clue: Something done with a casket when emptied (3)

indicatorNotes.when emptied: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written
CASKET without its middle ASKE

annotation.surface: Something that happens to a coffin once it has been cleared out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a burial rite, but the casket is only a word to be hollowed out.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a deed, as in 'an act of kindness'.

entries.clue: Danger! Use plastic garment (9)

indicatorNotes.plastic: plastic means mouldable, so the letters can be reshaped

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A safety warning on a plastic item of clothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' seems to describe the garment, but it is telling you the letters are mouldable.
annotation.definitionFit: Dungarees are a garment: trousers with a bib and shoulder straps.

entries.clue: Year in quality NI county (6)

indicatorNotes.in: in puts YR inside the word for quality

blocks.note: tone = quality, as of a voice or sound
yr is the usual abbreviation for year

annotation.surface: A fine year in a Northern Irish county.
annotation.walkthrough: NI is the standard short form of Northern Ireland, which is divided into six counties.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, in the west of the province.

entries.clue: Shelter respecting nurse (7)

blocks.note: re is Latin 'in the matter of', so respecting or concerning, as in memo headers
to nurse a patient is to treat them

annotation.surface: A refuge that looks after its nurses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nurse' is a verb here, not the person in uniform.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a place you withdraw to for shelter and quiet.

entries.clue: Only street on which cashpoint has nothing (2,4)

blocks.note: cashpoint is the British word for a cash machine, an ATM
O looks like a zero; 'has' attaches it to the cashpoint
St is the usual abbreviation for street

annotation.surface: The only road where the cash machine is empty.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes an empty cash machine the news, but 'Only' is the definition: think 'at most', no more than.
annotation.definitionFit: 'At most five' means only five and no more.

entries.clue: Rolled oats make fast hot snack (7)

indicatorNotes.Rolled: rolled oats are flattened and reshaped, so OATS is rearranged

blocks.note: OATS rearranged
to make fast is to tie securely

annotation.surface: Rolled oats as a quick warm breakfast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rolled oats' is a real breakfast food, so 'Rolled' hides as a description; 'make fast' means secure, not hurry. A toastie is a toasted sandwich.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the British name for a toasted sandwich, eaten hot as a snack.

entries.clue: Tape, pen or other means of recording ideas (9)

indicatorNotes.other: other means different, so the letters are made into something different

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A list of ways to get your thoughts down: a recorder, a pen, or something else.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Other' reads as 'or something else' in the list, but it is telling you to make the letters into another word.
annotation.definitionFit: Notepaper is what you write ideas down on.

entries.clue: Sniffy agency interested in space and light primarily (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of light is used

blocks.note: NASA is the US space agency
first letter of light

annotation.surface: A snooty organisation that cares about space and light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sniffy' seems to mean snooty, but it is taken literally: to do with sniffing, so to do with the nose.
annotation.definitionFit: Nasal means relating to the nose, the organ you sniff with.

entries.clue: Money girl? (5)

blocks.note: the smallest British coin
a short form of Penelope

annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'girl' only works as an example: Penny is one girl's name among many.
annotation.definitionFit: A penny is a small unit of money, and Penny a girl's name.

entries.clue: Processed meat cut in health resort (3)

indicatorNotes.cut: cut means shortened, so the last letter of SPAM goes

blocks.note: Spam is a brand of processed tinned meat

annotation.surface: Processed meat being sliced at a wellness retreat.
annotation.walkthrough: SPAM loses its M to leave the resort.
annotation.definitionFit: A spa is a health resort, originally one built around mineral springs.

entries.clue: Last of pizzas, American hot one — take-away choice? (5)

indicatorNotes.Last of: last of means only the final letter of pizzas is used

blocks.note: last letter of pizzas
US = American
H = hot, as on taps
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Deciding on the final pizza, an American Hot, for a takeaway order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American Hot' is a real pizza on British menus, so the surface reads as one order; the question mark flags sushi as just one example of a takeaway.
annotation.definitionFit: Sushi is a common takeaway meal.

entries.clue: Crushes relative by marriage (7)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Crushes' is a verb for a two-word phrase; the answer is a noun.

blocks.note: a verb here: treads down underfoot, a two-word phrase
your husband's or wife's boy from an earlier relationship

annotation.surface: Someone's in-law is the object of their infatuation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crushes' looks like the noun, romantic infatuations, but it is the verb: STEPS ON, which runs together as STEPSON.
annotation.definitionFit: A stepson is the son of your husband or wife, so a relative by marriage.

entries.clue: Adjust radio: eventually signal established then, first of all (5)

indicatorNotes.first of all: first of all means the first letter of each of the words

blocks.note: Radio Eventually Signal Established Then

annotation.surface: Tuning a radio until the signal finally locks on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Adjust radio' reads as one instruction, but 'Adjust' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To reset something is to adjust it back to a setting.

entries.clue: Dish without starter — still to come? (4)

indicatorNotes.without starter: a starter is what comes first, so the first letter of PLATE goes

blocks.note: a plate = a dish

annotation.surface: A meal served without its first course, the rest still on its way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Starter' is a first course in the meal picture, and the first letter in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Something late has not arrived yet, so it is still to come.

entries.clue: Sound of someone eating may blow up! (8)

indicatorNotes.Sound of: sound of points to how the words are said

blocks.note: a diner is someone eating; might = may

annotation.surface: A warning that the noise of a person eating could be explosive.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a joke about a noisy eater; 'blow up' is the definition, with dynamite as a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun used as a verb: to destroy with explosives, as in 'they dynamited the bridge'.
